notes.text:
# Status and retained original problem

Original P16.4 remains open in this submission. The new results are the target lemmas and estimates numbered 1–6, the generic-incidence construction with explicit initial point hypotheses numbered 7–10, and the local Cartier and section-lifting propositions 12–13. The finite graph theorem 11 is independently reconstructed. These results do not constitute an unconditional all-genus curve equation or an arbitrary-dimensional existence-and-uniqueness theorem. In particular, none of the unreviewed ROOT observations or native191 conclusions is a mathematical prerequisite. The submission has `candidate=false`.

The unchanged original domain is a complete characteristic-zero, residue-characteristic-zero, real-valued non-Archimedean field $K$, a smooth geometrically integral projective $K$-variety $X$ of arbitrary dimension $n$, and its actual ample rational line bundle $L$. Trivial, nontrivial, discrete, nondiscrete, and non-algebraically-closed fields remain included. Write $T=X^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $V=(L^n)>0$. The target is an arbitrary positive Radon measure of raw mass $V$, with the intrinsic finite-energy condition that it integrate every actual finite-energy potential. All psh metrics mean actual all-point decreasing Fubini–Study net endpoints on this bundle; literal values $-\infty$ and supported analytic points are retained. A scalar potential $u$ represents the absolute metric $\psi+u$ for a continuous psh reference $\psi$.

For continuous psh potentials the raw relative energy is
$$
 E(u)=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{j=0}^n\int_T u\,\operatorname{MA}(u^{[j]},0^{[n-j]}).
$$
On an actual singular endpoint its extension is
$$
 E(u)=\inf\{E(v):v\geq u,\ v\text{ continuous actual psh}\},\qquad
 \mathcal E^1=\{u:E(u)>-\infty\}.
$$
The operator used throughout is the genuine operator granted in O, with mass $V$. No inverse target construction is substituted for that operator. For a raw-mass target set
$$
 J(\mu)=\sup_{v\text{ continuous actual psh}}
              \left(E(v)-\int_T v\,d\mu\right).
$$
Constants cancel because $E(v+c)=E(v)+cV$. P16.3, P16.5, and P16.7 are not altered. Dimension zero is the one-point case with $V=1$; all new substantive arguments below have $n\geq1$.

# Exact mathematical prerequisites

The six accepted caller grants, including every supplied clarification, are used only in their stated scopes. Their full bodies are extracted verbatim from the supplied assignment into `sources/grant-O.tex`, `grant-D.tex`, `grant-N.tex`, `grant-T.tex`, `grant-Q.tex`, and `grant-C.tex`; the clarification files accompany them. `input.json` preserves the complete input. These mathematical labels are not registered note IDs. Local note n1 records their allowed use; supporting note lists contain only emitted local IDs.

O supplies the actual positive mixed $\mathcal E^1$ operator, all-test integrability against outputs, weighted decreasing continuity on arbitrary directed nets, extended energy continuity including $-\infty$, concavity, translation and monotonicity, admissible convex curvature calculus, actual segment differentiation, reference covariance, and complete-field pushforward. Its normalization clarification is retained; we never assume a nonpositive endpoint has nonpositive defining approximants. D supplies invariant actual descent, extended energy equality, invariant Radon lift, and continuous-dual identity for the completed algebraic closure. It supplies neither arbitrary noninvariant singular-test descent nor general equation existence. N requires an already actual continuous single-atom norming reference; coercivity is not attainment. T covers the full ample trivial-field equation. Q covers the split projective-line equation and its local disk geometry. C supplies strict locality and comparison. No additional equation, compactness, envelope, or uniqueness result is inferred from these labels.

The proofs in Sections 3–6 use O and elementary compact Radon theory. The generic-incidence proof uses explicitly stated actual point data and ordinary algebraic foundations, with a separate cohomological hypothesis for its independent complete-intersection proof. The node proof uses an explicitly specified actual split semistable cover. The section-lifting proof states the exact cohomology, completeness, and analytic/algebraic section-identification premises it needs. Their applicability to every original model is not asserted.

notes.summary: From O alone: finite continuous dual implies all-E1 integrability; all-E1 integrability iff a finite unit-energy bound; outputs have finite dual and attain it. General converse/coercivity still needs a proved uniform reference-integral bound.
notes.detailedSummary: For positive Radon mass V targets, increasing continuous Radon nets pass to the integral by compact inner approximation. The finite dual thus controls every actual E1 endpoint. A convex-series and directed FS-majorant construction proves uniform unit-energy control without a common anchor, excluding total collapse before invoking extended energy. The exact bound is B(tu)<=t A0(u)+n(n+1)t^2 B(u)/2. A0<=M0 would imply the intrinsic/dual equivalence and sublinear coercivity, but M0 is not proved generally. Every already genuine output MA(w) unconditionally has J=E(w)-integral w MA(w), attained by w; this is not prescribed-target existence.
notes.text:
Use precisely the original domain, actual cone, raw energy and operator in n1. No norming point or normalized-family compactness is assumed.

# Directed continuous Radon integration

**Lemma 1.** Let $\lambda$ be a finite Radon measure on a compact Hausdorff space. If $g_\alpha$ is a directed increasing net of nonnegative continuous functions and $g=\sup_\alpha g_\alpha$, then
$$
 \int g\,d\lambda=\sup_\alpha\int g_\alpha\,d\lambda.
$$

**Proof.** For each $t\geq0$, $U_t=\{g>t\}$ is the union of the directed open sets $U_{\alpha,t}=\{g_\alpha>t\}$. Any compact subset of $U_t$ has a finite subcover by these open sets; directedness puts that finite subcover inside one $U_{\alpha,t}$. Inner regularity gives $\lambda(U_t)=\sup_\alpha\lambda(U_{\alpha,t})$. For a finite height cutoff and a finite lower step approximation to the layer integral, choose a single index that approximates all its finitely many open-level masses. Its integral is at least the resulting step sum. Refining the steps and increasing the cutoff proves the reverse inequality to the immediate monotone bound. This proves the formula including an infinite integral. It is not a monotone-convergence assertion for arbitrary measurable nets. $\square$

# Finite continuous dual implies the intrinsic condition

**Theorem 2.** In the full original domain, $J(\mu)<\infty$ implies that every actual $u\in\mathcal E^1$ is absolutely $\mu$-integrable and that its pole set has zero $\mu$-mass. The supremum of the objective over actual $\mathcal E^1$ equals $J(\mu)$.

**Proof.** Choose a defining continuous FS net $f_\alpha\downarrow u$. Restrict to a tail dominated by one continuous stage and hence by a finite constant $M$. The nonnegative continuous functions $M-f_\alpha$ increase to the lower semicontinuous function $M-u$. By the dual inequality and O's energy monotonicity,
$$
 \int_T(M-f_\alpha)\,d\mu
 \leq MV+J(\mu)-E(f_\alpha)
 \leq MV+J(\mu)-E(u)<\infty.
$$
Lemma 1 gives the same finite bound for $\int(M-u)d\mu$. Since $u$ is bounded above, this proves absolute integrability and the pole assertion. The same lemma now gives convergence of the integrals. O's extended decreasing-energy continuity gives $E(f_\alpha)\downarrow E(u)$. Consequently
$$
 E(u)-\int_Tu\,d\mu
   =\lim_\alpha\left(E(f_\alpha)-\int_Tf_\alpha\,d\mu\right)\leq J(\mu).
$$
Continuous tests belong to $\mathcal E^1$, giving the reverse supremum inequality. No norming point, normalized-family compactness, or envelope theorem is used. $\square$

# A unit-energy bound without an anchor

Normalize an actual finite-energy potential by its finite supremum, so $u\leq0$ and $\sup_Tu=0$. Put
$$
 B(u)=-E(u)\geq0,\qquad I_\mu(u)=\int_T(-u)\,d\mu,
$$
initially allowing $I_\mu(u)=\infty$, and set
$$
 U_\mu=\sup\{I_\mu(u):u\in\mathcal E^1,\ \sup_Tu=0,\ B(u)\leq1\}.
$$

**Theorem 3.** In the full original domain, integrability of every actual $\mathcal E^1$ potential is equivalent to $U_\mu<\infty$. If $U_\mu$ is finite, then every normalized $u$ satisfies
$$
 I_\mu(u)\leq U_\mu\max\{1,B(u)\}.
$$
This linear estimate alone does not imply finite continuous dual.

**Proof.** Suppose all actual tests are integrable but $U_\mu=\infty$. Choose normalized $u_j$ with $B(u_j)\leq1$ and $I_\mu(u_j)\geq4^j$. Let
$$
 v_N=\sum_{j=1}^N2^{-j}u_j+2^{-N}0.
$$
O's convexity and concavity give actual finite-energy $v_N$, $v_{N+1}\leq v_N\leq0$, and $E(v_N)\geq-\sum_{j=1}^N2^{-j}\geq-1$. Let $v=\inf_Nv_N$ at every point. This limit is not identically $-\infty$. Otherwise, for $M>1/V$, the nested closed sets $\{v_N\geq-M\}$ would have empty intersection. Compactness gives an empty member, hence $v_N<-M$ everywhere and, by monotonicity, $E(v_N)\leq E(-M)=-MV<-1$, a contradiction. This is compactness of the underlying analytic carrier, not compactness of a normalized psh family.

Here is an explicit actual FS recognition of this endpoint, avoiding a diagonal sequence on a nonmetrizable space. Let $\mathcal F$ contain all continuous weighted FS scalars $f$ for which $f\geq v_N+\epsilon$ for some $N$ and $\epsilon>0$. It is nonempty: add $\epsilon$ to a defining FS approximant of $v_N$. Every member majorizes $v$. For any fixed $N$, those shifted approximants have infimum $v_N$ as the shift tends to zero, so $\inf\mathcal F=v$ pointwise.

The family is downward directed. Given $f\geq v_N+\epsilon$ and $g\geq v_M+\delta$, choose $L\geq\max(N,M)$ and $0<\eta<\min(\epsilon,\delta)/4$. A defining continuous FS net $h_\alpha\downarrow v_L$ eventually satisfies $h_\alpha\leq\min(f,g)-2\eta$ on the whole compact carrier: its closed upper-level sets against the continuous function $\min(f,g)-2\eta$ decrease to the empty set, because the endpoint has a strictly positive gap. Then $h_\alpha+\eta$ belongs to $\mathcal F$ and lies below both $f,g$. Ordered by reverse pointwise inequality, $\mathcal F$ therefore defines an actual decreasing FS net to $v$. Quotient equal functions if a partial order is desired.

Thus $v$ is a nontrivial actual psh endpoint. Every $f\in\mathcal F$ has $E(f)\geq E(v_N+\epsilon)\geq-1$. O's **extended** decreasing-energy continuity, applied before asserting $\mathcal E^1$ membership, gives $E(v)=\inf_{\mathcal F}E(f)\geq-1$. Hence $v\in\mathcal E^1$. Ordinary sequential monotone convergence now gives
$$
 I_\mu(v)=\sum_{j=1}^\infty2^{-j}I_\mu(u_j)
          \geq\sum_{j=1}^\infty2^j=\infty,
$$
contradicting the hypothesis.

Conversely, if $U_\mu<\infty$, O's concavity gives $B(tu)\leq tB(u)$ for $0<t\leq1$. Take $t=1$ when $B(u)\leq1$ and $t=1/B(u)$ otherwise. The scaled actual potential has supremum zero and cost at most one. Nonnegative integration gives $tI_\mu(u)=I_\mu(tu)\leq U_\mu$, proving the estimate and finiteness. Other potentials differ by a finite constant. $\square$

# The exact scaling bound and the missing geometric estimate

**Proposition 4.** For every normalized actual $u\in\mathcal E^1$, set
$$
 A_k(u)=\int_T(-u)\,\operatorname{MA}(u^{[k]},0^{[n-k]}),\qquad
 C_n=\frac{n(n+1)}2.
$$
Then all $A_k$ are finite nonnegative, $B=(n+1)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^nA_k$, and
$$
 B(tu)\leq tA_0(u)+C_nt^2B(u)\qquad(0\leq t\leq1).
$$

**Proof.** O supplies the finite integrals, genuine energy identity, and affine curvature calculus. For $0<t\leq1$ their finite positive expansion is
$$
 B(tu)=\frac t{n+1}\sum_{j=0}^n\sum_{k=0}^j
       \binom jk t^k(1-t)^{j-k}A_k(u).
$$
The $k=0$ terms sum to at most $tA_0$. For $k\geq1$, $A_k\leq(n+1)B$ and the binomial weight in the $j$th sum is $1-(1-t)^j\leq jt$. Their total is at most $tB\sum_{j=0}^n jt=C_nt^2B$. At $t=0$ use the reference potential itself; no zero multiple of a pole is evaluated. $\square$

**Corollary 5, conditional on a uniform reference bound.** Suppose, additionally, that there is a proved finite $M_0$ with $A_0(u)\leq M_0$ for every normalized actual finite-energy potential on the reference and bundle under consideration. Then the intrinsic condition, $U_\mu<\infty$, and $J(\mu)<\infty$ are equivalent. With
$$
 c=2(M_0+1+\sqrt{C_n}),\qquad A=cU_\mu,
$$
one has
$$
 I_\mu(u)\leq A(1+\sqrt{B(u)}),\qquad
 E(u)-\int u\,d\mu\leq-B(u)+A(1+\sqrt{B(u)}),\qquad
 J(\mu)\leq A+\frac{A^2}4.
$$

**Proof.** Take $t=[c(1+\sqrt{B(u)})]^{-1}$. Then $0<t\leq1$, $tM_0\leq1/2$, and $C_nt^2B(u)\leq1/4$. Proposition 4 gives $B(tu)\leq3/4$. Theorem 3's unit bound gives $tI_\mu(u)\leq U_\mu$ and the displayed estimates. Maximizing $-b+A\sqrt b$ over $b\geq0$ gives $A^2/4$. Theorem 2 and Theorem 3 supply the other implications. The objective tends to $-\infty$ when $B\to\infty$. This proves coercivity, not attainment. The required $M_0$ has **not** been proved for all original varieties here. $\square$

There is an unconditional necessary-target conclusion which does not require $M_0$.

**Corollary 6.** Every genuine output $\mu=\operatorname{MA}(w)$, $w\in\mathcal E^1$, has finite continuous dual, and $w$ attains the objective supremum over all actual $\mathcal E^1$:
$$
 J(\mu)=E(w)-\int_Tw\,d\mu<\infty.
$$

**Proof.** O integrates every actual test against this output. Concavity of the actual segment energy and its derivative at $w$ give
$$
 E(v)-E(w)\leq\int_T(v-w)\,d\mu
$$
for every actual $v\in\mathcal E^1$. Each integral is finite on a common finite-value full-measure set; common pole values are never subtracted. This bounds every objective by the displayed finite value. Continuous majorants $w_\alpha\downarrow w$ converge in energy and in their integrals against the fixed output by O's weighted law, so the continuous supremum has this value as well. This proves a necessary condition and an attainment statement for already known outputs. It does not construct an output for an arbitrary prescribed intrinsic target. $\square$

notes.summary: Actual generic-incidence points on one common complete coefficient-Gauss field, with exact section-value preservation; requires explicit maximal-residue coordinate hypotheses and (H), and does not establish the general Shilov estimate.
notes.detailedSummary: For finitely many honest generic-support points over complete algebraically closed nontrivial C, integral embedding coordinates must generate a residual dimension-n subfield and the full residual dimension must be n. A Jacobian block argument proves independence of all solved and free hyperplane coefficients, giving the same coefficient-Gauss F at every point. With explicit negative-twist cohomology vanishing (H), incidence smoothness and the Koszul complex prove a geometrically integral actual curve of degree m^(n-1)V. Its points have completed residue field H_i(A_free)^ and residual degree one, with original values preserved. Algebraic-closure lifts are constructed directly; GM A.7 is not misused for F/C. Initial model/Shilov hypotheses, actual semistable core and raw curvature estimates remain unproved.
notes.text:
# Actual generic incidence: hypotheses and common field

The following construction is separate from any unproved Shilov-model assertion. Let $C$ be complete, algebraically closed, nontrivially valued, of characteristic and residue characteristic zero. Let $X/C$ be smooth geometrically integral projective of dimension $n\geq2$. Clear rational denominators and choose an actual very ample $M=mL$, with an embedding given by $S_0,\ldots,S_N$. Put $g_l=S_l/S_0$ on the affine chart $S_0\ne0$.

Assume finitely many actual points $y_i$ have generic scheme support and satisfy the following explicit point hypotheses:

* $|g_l(y_i)|\leq1$ for every $l$;
* the reductions of the $g_l(y_i)$ generate a subfield $k(Y_i)\subset\widetilde{\mathcal H(y_i)}$, of transcendence degree $n$ over $k=\widetilde C$, and are coordinates of an integral affine $k$-variety $Y_i$;
* $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\widetilde{\mathcal H(y_i)}=n$.

Equality of $k(Y_i)$ with the whole completed residue field's residue is not required. These are initial hypotheses. This paper does not prove they hold for every Shilov point of a suitable actual model reference.

Set $s=n-1$, $r'=sN$, and $r=s(N+1)$. Let $H_i=\mathcal H(y_i)$, the completion of the honest valued field $C(X)$. Introduce $r'$ free variables $A_{jl}$ ($1\leq j\leq s$, $1\leq l\leq N$) with unit-radius Gauss norm over $H_i$, and complete to $H'_i$. Define in this field
$$
 A_{j0}=-\sum_{l=1}^N A_{jl}g_l(y_i).
$$

**Lemma 7, residual independence.** All $r$ parameters, including the solved $A_{j0}$, have algebraically independent residues over $k$.

**Proof.** Consider the algebraic map
$$
 Y_i\times\mathbb A^{r'}_k\longrightarrow\mathbb A^r_k,
 \quad (y,a)\longmapsto\bigl(a_{jl},-\sum_l a_{jl}\bar g_l(y)\bigr).
$$
The integral variety $Y_i$ has a nonempty smooth locus in characteristic zero. The coordinate functions $\bar g_l$ give its closed affine embedding, so at a smooth point their differentials span its $n$-dimensional cotangent space. Choose $s$ independent linear combinations of these differentials. At the corresponding coefficient rows, the differential of the displayed map has the identity block on all $r'$ free coordinates and an additional rank-$s$ block in the $Y_i$ directions. Hence an $r$-minor is nonzero at that point, and at the generic point. In characteristic zero, $r$ independent differentials of functions imply their algebraic independence: the rank of the differentials of a subfield equals its transcendence degree, by choosing a transcendence basis and using separability of algebraic extensions. Thus the map is dominant and the $r$ output functions are algebraically independent in $k(Y_i)(A_{\mathrm{free}})$. Its injection into $\widetilde H_i(A_{\mathrm{free}})$ preserves that assertion. $\square$

**Lemma 8, the same complete coefficient-Gauss field.** Let
$$
 F=\widehat{C(A_{jl}:1\leq j\leq s,\ 0\leq l\leq N)}
$$
with the unit coefficient-Gauss norm on all $r$ independent symbols. The preceding evaluation embeds this **same** complete field $F$ isometrically in every $H'_i$.

**Proof.** Each full parameter is integral and its residue is a nonzero member of an independent family, hence its norm is one. For any nonzero polynomial over $C$, divide by a coefficient of maximal norm. Its reduction is a nonzero polynomial over $k$ and cannot vanish on the independent residues from Lemma 7. The evaluation therefore has norm exactly one after normalization, proving the coefficient-Gauss identity. Fractions retain their quotient norms, so the rational function field map is injective and isometric. Completeness extends it uniquely and isometrically to $F$. The formulas representing the solved coefficients can differ with $i$; the domain field and its norm are identical. Completion of a valued field changes neither its residue field nor its value group: approximating a nonzero completed element to strictly smaller error preserves its norm and, after unit normalization, its residue. In particular $\widetilde F=k(A_{\mathrm{all}})$ and $\widetilde H'_i=\widetilde H_i(A_{\mathrm{free}})$. $\square$

# A complete-intersection proof with an explicit cohomological premise

For an independent proof of geometric integrality, impose the following finite cohomological hypothesis on the chosen actual embedding power:
$$
 H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(-kM))=0
 \quad(1\leq k\leq n-1,\ 1\leq q\leq n-1). \tag{H}
$$
This is an explicit premise of the construction as formulated here. Smooth-projective Serre duality and Serre vanishing give such sufficiently large powers; their complete recursive proofs are not newly supplied in this paper. No unverified model cohomology vanishing over $C^\circ/a$ is substituted for (H). Alternatively, the complete generic Bertini primary units in the ledger give a source route to geometric irreducibility. We record their foundations separately instead of declaring them new caller grants.

**Proposition 9.** Under (H), the $s=n-1$ full generic hyperplanes
$$
 A_{j0}S_0+\sum_{l=1}^NA_{jl}S_l=0\quad(1\leq j\leq s)
$$
cut out a smooth geometrically integral projective curve $D$ over $F$. Its actual restricted bundle has raw degree
$$
 a=\deg(L|_D)=m^{n-1}(L^n).
$$

**Proof.** First work over the rational coefficient field $E=C(A_{\mathrm{all}})$. Here the coefficients are the full independent generic coefficients, not a fixed projection subsystem. For a smooth embedded projective variety $Z$ of dimension $d$, the conditions that a hyperplane section vanish and have zero differential at a specified point impose $d+1$ independent linear conditions on its coefficients. Indeed choose a nonvanishing embedding section as local frame; the resulting affine coordinate functions span the cotangent space. The incidence of such bad pairs therefore has dimension $N-1$ over the parameter space of projective hyperplanes of dimension $N$. Its projection is closed because $Z$ is projective. It misses the generic hyperplane. The calculation also holds after algebraic closure. Thus the generic section is geometrically smooth. On each positive-dimensional component the generic hyperplane neither contains the component nor misses it, by the projective intersection dimension theorem; its intersection has dimension $d-1$.

Apply this argument successively with the independent rows of full coefficients. Each intermediate intersection is smooth, has the expected dimension, and the next equation is nonzero on every component. The equations form a regular sequence; its Koszul complex gives a resolution of the final structure sheaf by finite direct sums of $\mathcal O_X(-kM)$, $1\leq k\leq s$. For clarity, the degree-zero hypercohomology of this resolution has only $H^0(\mathcal O_X)$ contributing: a term $\mathcal O_X(-kM)$ lies in degree $-k$ and would require $H^k$ to contribute to degree zero, or $H^{k-1}$ to map into it. These vanish by (H) and $H^0$ of a negative ample bundle is zero. Therefore $H^0(D_E,\mathcal O_{D_E})=E$. Cohomology commutes with extension of the base field: a finite affine Čech cover of a separated scheme has affine intersections, and tensoring its complex with a field is exact. The same vanishings and equality hold over an algebraic closure and over the completion $F$.

The geometrically smooth projective final curve has no nilpotents, and different irreducible components of a smooth curve are disjoint. If there were two geometric components, they would give a nontrivial idempotent in its global functions. The equality just proved excludes this. It is therefore geometrically integral. The same Čech and geometric base-extension argument preserves this conclusion over $F$. Each equation is an actual section of the actual $M$ on $X_F$, so the regular-sequence intersection class is $M^{n-1}$, and intersecting it with $L$ gives the displayed raw degree. Rational powers were cleared before defining this embedding. $\square$

The dimension and cotangent foundations in this proof are ordinary algebraic foundations, not a proof of the formal model assertions R1–R5. The cohomological premise makes explicit where a sufficiently high embedding power is used. In particular the generic curve is not claimed to be genus zero.

# Actual incidence points and exact preservation of original values

**Theorem 10.** Under the preceding point hypotheses and (H), there is an actual analytic point $y'_i\in D^{\mathrm{an}}$ over each $y_i$, with
$$
 \mathcal H(y'_i)=H'_i,\qquad
 \operatorname{trdeg}_{\widetilde F}\widetilde{\mathcal H(y'_i)}=1,
 \qquad |\mathcal H(y'_i)^\times|=|F^\times|=|C^\times|.
$$
Every original rational-function value, and every original section norm in a pulled-back continuous metric, is preserved. No point of a curve over the unchanged ground field is asserted.

**Proof.** In the affine chart the map $F[g_1,\ldots,g_N]\to H'_i$ given by the original evaluations kills all the hyperplane equations, by their defining solved coefficients. Hence it defines a multiplicative seminorm on the actual coordinate algebra of $D$; this is an analytic point. Restricted to the original $C$-coordinate algebra it is exactly $y_i$.

The kernel on the integral curve algebra is zero. To see this without assuming a function-field injection in advance, its seminorm residue field contains the reductions of the original $g_l$ and the free parameters. These generate $k(Y_i)(A_{\mathrm{free}})$, of transcendence degree $n+r'$ over $k$. The base residue field is $\widetilde F=k(A_{\mathrm{all}})$, of transcendence degree $r=r'+n-1$; it lies in that same field by the incidence formulas. Thus the point's residue has relative transcendence degree at least one. A nongeneric point of an integral affine $F$-curve is closed and has finite residue extension of $F$. The valuation residue of a finite valued extension is algebraic: lifts of a residue-field linearly independent finite set are linearly independent over the base field, after normalizing a relation by a maximal coefficient. Its residual transcendence degree is zero. This contradiction proves generic support and injection of $F(D)$.

The image of $F(D)$ contains $C(X)$ and all free coefficient variables. Indeed the $g_l$ generate the original affine coordinate ring's function field. Since $y_i$ has generic support, $C(X)$ is dense in $H_i$ by the definition of its completed residue field. Polynomials in the free variables with coefficients in $H_i$ are Gauss-approximated by polynomials with coefficients in $C(X)$, by approximating their finitely many coefficients. For a nonzero denominator, a sufficiently small approximation error preserves its norm and controls its inverse. Thus $C(X)(A_{\mathrm{free}})$ is dense in $H_i(A_{\mathrm{free}})$ and in its completion $H'_i$. The completed residue field of the point, being the closure of $F(D)$ in $H'_i$, is exactly $H'_i$.

The residue formula in Lemma 8 and the initial maximal residual dimension give
$$
 \operatorname{trdeg}_{\widetilde F}\widetilde H'_i
    =(n+r')-(r'+n-1)=1.
$$
There is no need for equality $\widetilde H_i=k(Y_i)$. All free Gauss variables have norm one. Here is the elementary valuation independence bound used for the value group. Choose units with $d$ independent residues, and field elements with $q$ rationally independent values modulo the base value group. A polynomial in these elements can be grouped by the exponents of the latter $q$ elements. Within each group, divide its coefficient polynomial in the units by a base coefficient of maximal norm; independent residues make that coefficient polynomial's norm exactly the maximal coefficient norm. Different groups have different valuations, since their value differences cannot lie in the base group. A unique least valuation therefore survives in any nonzero polynomial. Thus the $d+q$ chosen elements are algebraically independent, and $d+q\leq n$ in $C(X)$. Residue and group are unchanged by completion. Taking $d=n$ shows the value-group extension is torsion. Since $C$ has divisible value group, an ordered torsion extension inside $\mathbb R$ of that subgroup has no new element: if an integer multiple of a real value belongs to the subgroup, division by that integer puts the value itself there. Consequently $|H_i^\times|=|C^\times|$, and the unit Gauss extension and completion preserve this equality.

Finally, $H_i\hookrightarrow H'_i$ is isometric. Evaluation of every original rational function is unchanged. For an original section, use a local rational frame nonvanishing at the generic support; its coefficient norm is unchanged, and the pulled-back metric's frame norm is its original value. This proves the section assertion. $\square$

There is also an actual completed-algebraic-closure lift preserving these invariants. Put $B=\widehat{\overline F}$. Extend $F\hookrightarrow H'_i$ to an embedding of an algebraic closure into an algebraic closure of $H'_i$; uniqueness of the extension of the valuation from the complete field $F$ makes it isometric. It extends to $B\hookrightarrow\Omega_i=\widehat{\overline{H'_i}}$. The original coordinate evaluations now define a point $z_i\in D_B^{\mathrm{an}}$. The injection of the old $F(D)$ survives evaluation, so its closure $H'_i$ embeds in $\mathcal H(z_i)$. Residues of $\Omega_i$ are algebraic over $\widetilde H'_i$, and $\widetilde B$ is algebraic over $\widetilde F$: algebraic valuation extensions have algebraic residue, and completion changes no residue. The residue of this point thus has transcendence degree one over $\widetilde B$. The same closed-point argument as above proves its generic support before using $B(D)$. Its completed residue field is then exactly the closure of $B(D)$ in $\Omega_i$. The value group stays the original divisible group. These are the usual type-II invariants on an algebraically closed curve. Recognition by a semistable model still uses the curve geometry and formal/reduction foundations audited below. GM A.7 has **not** been applied to the initial transcendental extension $F/C$; its stated domain is algebraic-completion extensions only.

Theorem 10 constructs the same coefficient-Gauss base at every selected original point and preserves actual values. It does not prove the initial Shilov hypotheses, semistable containment of the selected lifts, the raw curve curvature formula for all already actual restricted metrics, or the uniform $M_0$ required in Corollary 5.

notes.detailedSummary: For every finite connected weighted graph with lengths in a nonzero divisible subgroup, signed starting vertex curvature and nonnegative target of the same positive raw mass, anchored Laplacian solutions admit uniformly convergent rational-slope value-group approximants after subdivision, positive at every refined vertex. notes.text:
# Positive rational-slope interpolation with irrational cycles

**Theorem 11, a finite graph theorem.** Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R$ be a nonzero divisible subgroup. Let $G$ be a finite connected metric graph with edge lengths in $\Lambda$ and fixed positive real weights $w_e$. Let $\theta$ be a signed vertex measure and $\mu$ a nonnegative vertex measure, both of mass $V>0$. For a vertex $z$ there is a unique edge-affine $F$ with $F(z)=0$ and $\theta+\Delta F=\mu$, where $\Delta$ is weighted outgoing slope. There are subdivisions and rational-slope functions $G_j$ with all vertex values in $\Lambda$, one common denominator at each stage, $G_j\to F$ uniformly, $\theta+\Delta G_j\geq0$, and $\theta+\Delta G_j\to\mu$ weakly. Every vertex of the refined graph has strictly positive curvature at each stage.

**Proof.** Subdivide every self-loop at its midpoint, retaining the loop and giving the new vertex zero initial mass. For vertex values $h$, edgewise cancellation gives
$$
 -\sum_vh(v)\Delta h(v)=\sum_{e=ab}\frac{w_e}{\ell_e}(h(b)-h(a))^2.
$$
The matrix is symmetric with kernel exactly constants by connectivity, hence image the zero-sum vectors. This gives the anchored solution. A no-edge singleton has only the constant solution.

For the nontrivial graph, let $k$ be its number of vertices and replace $\mu$ by $\mu_\epsilon=(1-\epsilon)\mu+\epsilon(V/k)\sum_v\delta_v$. Its anchored solution $F_\epsilon$ converges to $F$, by finite-dimensional linearity, and every old vertex has a positive margin. Since $\mathbb Q a\subset\Lambda$ is dense for any nonzero $a\in\Lambda$, approximate the finitely many shared vertex values by $g_v\in\Lambda$, with $g_z=0$ and error at most $h$. On an oriented edge $a\to b$, write $d=g_b-g_a$, $c=d/\ell$. Choose rational $q_1<c<q_2$ as close to $c$ as desired. Set
$$
 t=\frac{d-q_2\ell}{q_1-q_2}\in\Lambda,\qquad 0<t<\ell.
$$
Use slope $q_1$ on the first subedge and $q_2$ on the second. The terminal value is exactly $g_b$, and the bend value $g_a+q_1t$ lies in $\Lambda$. Shared endpoint values guarantee exact compatibility around every cycle.

The bend contributes $w_e(q_2-q_1)>0$. The two endpoint contributions are $w_eq_1$ and $-w_eq_2$. Taking $h$ small enough and both rational slopes within $\eta$ of the original $F_\epsilon$ slope makes the error at each old vertex less than $\eta\sum_{e\ni v}w_e$. Choose this below half its positive margin. Thus all old and new curvature atoms are positive and their total mass remains $V$. The uniform function error is at most $h+\eta\max_e\ell_e$; the inserted mass tends to zero with $\eta$. Letting the errors and $\epsilon$ tend to zero gives both convergences. A finite common denominator clears every rational slope, with all scaled vertex values still in $\Lambda$. $\square$

The simpler fixed-edge rational-slope approach fails on two parallel edges of lengths $1$ and $\sqrt2$: their shared endpoint difference would have to lie in $\mathbb Q\cap\sqrt2\mathbb Q=\{0\}$. The positive movable bends are essential. For $\theta=(1,1)$, $\mu=(2,0)$, $\epsilon=1/10$, and $d=(9/10)(2-\sqrt2)$, slopes $52/100,53/100$ and $37/100,38/100$ give bend positions $-127+90\sqrt2$ and $-180+128\sqrt2$. The curvature is $189/100,9/100,1/100,1/100$, with total exactly $2$. The exact program independently checks these formulas and 81 specified variants. It supplies no actual formal model.

notes.text:
# A local actual vertical Cartier calculation

**Proposition 12, with explicit actual cover hypotheses.** Work over $R=C^\circ$ with $C$ complete algebraically closed and nontrivial. Suppose an actual proper split strict semistable formal curve has a node-and-vertex cover of the following form. A node block for an edge $a\to b$ is étale over
$$
 \operatorname{Spf}R\langle x,y\rangle/(xy-\pi_e),\qquad
 \ell_e=\operatorname{val}(\pi_e)>0.
$$
The endpoint $a$ has $\operatorname{val}(x)=0$, and $b$ has $\operatorname{val}(x)=\ell_e$. On intersections with the smooth vertex part at $a$, $x$ is a formal unit; at $b$, $y$ is a formal unit. Distinct node blocks meet through those smooth parts. The resulting reductions identify the residual branches as the usual parameters at their nodes, with no extra zeros or poles. Self-loops have first been subdivided, so their two branches remain present. Let $f$ be integral $\Lambda$-affine on the skeleton and constant on retraction fibres, with $f(v)\in\Lambda=\operatorname{val}(C^\times)$.

Then $f$ defines an actual vertical Cartier line bundle on this formal model, generically trivialized by $1$, of weight $f\circ r$. Its residual component degree at $v$ is $\Delta f(v)$ in the unweighted outgoing-slope convention. Tensoring an already actual formal bundle changes its actual residual degrees by these numbers and retains its actual generic bundle. Rational slopes are handled by clearing one common denominator.

**Proof.** Choose $c_v\in C^\times$ with valuation $f(v)$. On the smooth vertex block use the meromorphic equation $g_v=c_v$. On an oriented node block, where $f=f(a)+q\operatorname{val}(x)$ and $q\in\mathbb Z$, use $g_e=c_a x^q$. The constants $c_v$ and the coordinates $x,y$ are non-zero-divisors; $xy=\pi_e$ and flatness imply this for $x,y$. Negative exponents lie in the total meromorphic ring. They are all invertible on the generic fibre.

On the $a$ overlap, $g_e/g_a=x^q$ is a literal formal unit. On the $b$ overlap,
$$
 g_e/g_b=(c_a\pi_e^q/c_b)y^{-q}
$$
is a unit: the constant factor has valuation zero by $f(b)=f(a)+q\ell_e$, and $y$ is a formal unit there. Overlaps of node blocks reduce to these verified vertex ratios. They consequently satisfy the cocycle identity as ratios in a common meromorphic ring. This constructs the Cartier divisor $D$, rather than merely a function of norm one. In the local frame $g^{-1}$ of $\mathcal O(D)$, the canonical generic section $1$ has norm $|g|$, so its additive weight is $\operatorname{val}(g)=f\circ r$.

For the degree on component $C_a$, normalize its rational generic section by $1/c_a$. Near the node its coefficient in the local frame is $x^q$, so its reduction has order $q$ at that branch. For $C_b$, normalization by $1/c_b$ gives a unit times $y^{-q}$, hence order $-q$. On the smooth vertex part the coefficient is one; there are no other zeros or poles by the cover hypothesis. Summing the orders of a rational section on the normalization of each proper residual component gives its line-bundle degree. Thus the correction is the sum of outgoing slopes. Each edge's two corrections sum to zero; subdivisions and loops preserve the calculation. For $f/m$, apply the construction to $f$ and take the rational tensor power $1/m$. $\square$

This calculation is confined to this explicitly given actual cover. It does not prove global semistable domination, algebraization, the cover theorem itself, or the genuine raw component formula for the analytic Monge–Ampère operator. It avoids KRZB's analytic-meromorphic extension only for this vertical-monomial degree calculation; that extension is not declared unnecessary for other functions.

# Section lifting and actual pure FS recognition

**Proposition 13, with explicit cohomology and GAGA hypotheses.** Let $R=C^\circ$ and $0<|a|<1$. Suppose $\mathfrak X$ is a proper flat, $a$-adically complete, separated formal $R$-curve, locally with complete separated rings, and $\mathfrak A$ an actual formal invertible sheaf. Its generic analytification is identified with the original $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and $\mathfrak A$ there is identified with the actual $dL$ after clearing denominators. Assume for some $k\geq1$:

1. $\mathfrak A_0^k$ on $X_0=\mathfrak X\bmod a$ is generated by finitely many global sections and $H^1(X_0,\mathfrak A_0^k)=0$;
2. global analytic sections of its generic fibre coincide, under the given bundle identification, with algebraic sections of the actual $kdL$ on $X$.

Then the formal metric on $dL$ is an actual pure Fubini–Study metric, with the same bundle and no reference to a numerical replacement.

**Proof.** Put $A_r=\mathfrak A^k/a^{r+1}\mathfrak A^k$. Flatness and local freeness give identical associated-graded layers $a^r\mathfrak A^k/a^{r+1}\mathfrak A^k\simeq A_0$. Thus for every $r\geq1$ there is an exact sequence of sheaves
$$
 0\longrightarrow A_0\longrightarrow A_r\longrightarrow A_{r-1}\longrightarrow0.
$$
The single stated $H^1$ vanishing makes $H^0(A_r)\to H^0(A_{r-1})$ surjective for every $r$. Lift each of the finitely many chosen generating sections through all these maps, compatibly. Sheaf completeness identifies global sections of $\mathfrak A^k$ with the inverse limit of these sections; this follows from the defining complete local sheaves, since global sections commute with limits. The lifted sections generate the formal bundle. Locally, mod-$a$ generation allows a chosen frame coefficient $b$ to be written $\sum b_if_i+a b^{(1)}$. Repeating this on the successive error, with all coefficients integral, produces convergent $a$-adic sums of the $b_i$. Completeness gives $b=\sum b_if_i$ exactly. Hence the local generation assertion does not assume the ring is Noetherian.

On the generic fibre each lifted section is algebraic by assumption 2. They have no common zero by the formal generation. In a formal local frame the coefficient functions satisfy $|f_i|\leq1$. Integral coefficients in an identity $1=\sum b_if_i$ also have norm at most one, so at every analytic point $\max_i|f_i|=1$. The formal metric on $\mathfrak A^k$ therefore equals the metric defined by precisely these global sections with zero FS weights. Dividing by $k$ gives the metric on the actual $dL$, and by $d$ the rational metric on $L$. All identities hold at every point of the original carrier. $\square$

This lemma needs one vanishing on the **whole mod-$a$ fibre**, not only on the reduced residual curve. It also needs the actual generic-bundle identification and the stated analytic/algebraic section equality. Those inputs are not proved for every semistable model in this paper. If the mod-$a$ sections instead define a closed embedding and their standard-chart preimages are affine formal schemes, the same complete lifting argument makes the maps from completed projective chart rings surjective: lift a polynomial representative modulo $a$, subtract it, divide by $a$, and iterate. This gives a closed formal embedding. Algebraizing its coherent ideal still requires projective GFGA's coherence, full-faithfulness, and generation premises; this observation is not an algebraization theorem.

The potential difficulty is concrete. For a dense divisible value group choose $\operatorname{val}(a)=1$. For every $N$ there is $b_N$ with $\operatorname{val}(b_N)=1/(N+1)$. Its image in $R/aR$ is nilpotent, but $b_N^N\notin aR$. Thus the nilradical of $R/aR$ is not nilpotent. One may not justify whole mod-$a$ ampleness or uniform Serre vanishing by treating this fibre as a finite nilpotent thickening. A separate valid argument, for example a fully verified finitely presented Artinian descent, is needed.

# What the accessible primaries actually resolve

All 16 exact frozen primary files match their supplied bytes and SHA-256 hashes. All six extracted grant files also match the review-source hashes supplied with their clarifications. These checks verify provenance, not theorems. The quote-free ledger records whole printed proof units actually read, scan checks, application scopes, and recursive gaps. No prior retrieval failure is used to avoid an accessible primary.

The most relevant source facts and boundaries are as follows.

* BL85's complete Section 7 was read, including the two genus-at-least-one lemmas, the induction and the final algebraic reduction. The scanned pages 374–378 were inspected. Its theorem has a stable genus-at-least-two branch and a semistable genus-at-most-one branch. The affinoid $\mathbb P^1$ subdivision in its covering argument is explicitly omitted and refers to BGR. Earlier whole Lemma 3.5 and relevant preceding annular arguments were read and checked against scans. Their earlier reduction, genus, finite-map, and formal-fibre dependencies are not all reconstructed. An incomplete recursive audit is not an unconditional new semistable theorem.
* BPR's entire Theorem 4.11 proof 4.15 was read, including the one-edge and singleton cases, its supporting Lemmas 4.12 and 4.14, and its omitted analogous domination cases. Proposition 3.13 and the inverse-limit proof 5.2 were read. The latter invokes a separation assertion and compact inverse systems; it does not permit skipping the actual curve geometry. Formal fibres and canonical-model identification refer to BL85, Thuillier, and other foundations. Its Remark 4.2(2) cites Abbes for formal algebraization.
* GH B.7 and B.8 were read as complete printed proof units. They use reduction/unit recognition and global formal-chart constructions. Proposition 12 independently replaces only the vertical node/unit and residual-degree calculation under its stated actual cover hypotheses.
* KRZB Section 2.3 and Theorem 2.6 were read completely in their arbitrary complete algebraically closed nontrivial-field domain. The graph divisor is negative outgoing slope. Its footnote explicitly identifies the analytic extension beyond BPR's algebraic-function statement. No silent analytic extension is imported here. Its theorem excludes a singleton skeleton.
* BE's actual projective model-to-pure-FS theorem 5.14 and nef-model recognition 7.8/7.9 were read in full. The latter requires an actual projective model and actual ample generic bundle. Lemma 6.3 supplies a finite norming **set** of Shilov points, not a single atom or a uniform individual lower bound. Reduced-fibre cofinality 4.19–4.20 generates its own formal/reduction dependencies. GM 4.11/4.12 supplies ample algebraic domination only after the carrier is in its actual algebraic domain.
* GM Appendix A.5 and A.7 were read fully. A.5 recognizes maximal residual points using affinoid dimension and formal embedding foundations. A.7 is limited to algebraic-completion extensions; A.8 gives the warning for arbitrary extensions. Theorem 10 applies its elementary invariant calculation afresh on the actual generic curve, before the algebraic-completion step.
* GJKM's [FK88] is **Eberhard Freitag and Reinhardt Kiehl**, *Étale cohomology and the Weil conjecture* (1988), as its bibliography confirms. The source's Proposition I.10.3.2 citation under that label is preserved as a source citation, not identified with another book. Fujiwara–Kato arXiv:1308.4734v5 is a separately read alternative primary. All new references use these distinct identities. The historical native191 misidentification remains historical input data only.
* Fujiwara–Kato's whole Chapter 0 §9.2(a) proof and 8.5.21–25 were read. A rank-one complete valuation ring is $a$-adically complete and $a$-torsion-free: the valuation topology and $a$-adic topology have the same cofinal neighborhoods, and it is a domain. Corollary 9.2.7 and Theorem 8.5.25(2) therefore have the intended base domain; their finiteness proof uses Raynaud–Gruson or its stated alternative division argument. These are not Noetherian/discrete hypotheses. Their complete generated foundations have not all been audited here.
* The entire printed projective GFGA argument I.10.2(c), including 10.2.4–6 and the final presentation argument, was read. It establishes existence on completed projective space using coherence, uniform graded-layer vanishing, comparison/full-faithfulness, and algebraization of finite presentations. The general carving proof and its Lemma 10.2.2 are abbreviated. I.10.3.2 explicitly leaves the adapted EGA III 5.4.5 algebraization argument to the reader. Reading its statement and reduction is not reading that missing proof. II.9.4–9.5's printed proofs treat the stronger t.u. adhesive base case, and generate comparison, formal coherent lift, and GFGA dependencies. Proposition 13 keeps the remaining section-identification premise explicit.

The supplied suggesting route through closed formal projective embeddings is reasonable data to investigate. The preceding lifting proof verifies the repeated-section part once whole mod-$a$ generation and vanishing are known. It does not establish those premises, finite presentation/coherence of every required ideal, algebraization of the carrier, or all compatibilities of the actual generic bundle. We do not replace the omitted proof with an appeal to its statement.

# Remaining exact curve and higher-dimensional obligations

R1–R5 from native191 are not all discharged. In the curve sector, the remaining chain is: actual semistable domination of every required old bundle/model in the non-Noetherian domain; a global node cover and compatible refinements; whole mod-$a$ ampleness/vanishing or another verified actual same-bundle recognition; proper generic carrier and bundle identification; genuine raw component-degree curvature coefficients; complementary-ball frames and all terminal-point recovery; and an actual finite Galois orbit for the downstairs norming reference. Proposition 12 handles the explicit local Cartier and degree calculation. Proposition 13 handles section lifting and FS recognition with its stated premises. Neither turns an abstract graph distribution into an actual metric without them.

The generic-incidence theorem constructs actual points on a common auxiliary complete base under its initial residual-coordinate hypotheses, and preserves every original value. It does not yet verify those initial hypotheses for every finite reference Shilov set. The next missing step is an actual common semistable curve core and domination for the already actual restricted model/FS metrics, with the raw slope/curvature formula. A finite-core voltage estimate would then bound the reference Shilov values uniformly. Retain all graph loops: refinements of a fixed full core can add trees and subdivide its edges, and voltages extend constantly along attached trees. An abstract graph estimate without that actual realization does not supply $M_0$. No general intrinsic integrability-to-finite-dual theorem is claimed here without that bound.

Even a complete unconditional curve equation would leave the original dimension-$\geq2$ existence and every-solution all-point uniqueness requirements. O and C already supply the operator and comparison in the granted domain. T supplies the trivial boundary, and Q the split projective line. For the remaining original equation there is still no proved actual normalized-potential compactness or a replacement, no complete envelope/orthogonality and both-sign outer differentiation chain where that route needs it, no actual attainment for every prescribed intrinsic target, and no every-solution recovery at every point in arbitrary dimension. Corollary 6's attainment concerns an already known output, and Corollary 5's coercivity concerns a still conditional reference estimate. They do not establish the required antecedents. The exact original problem remains open.

`verify_packet.py` reads only the exact authorized manifest files, verifies their bindings, and extracts the six full grants and clarifications from `input.json`. `finite_checks.py` uses standard-library exact fractions and $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)$; it checks the displayed interpolation prototype and 81 specified positive-bend variants, finite Bernstein/scaling grids, raw curve normalization, and nilpotence examples.
